model_note: Fixed-step grid plus room hot-gas layers. Approximation for a residential fire demonstration, not a validated fire engineering or structural solver. Thin wall barriers separate cells. Mixed floor, wall finish, ceiling and furniture fuel in each cell share the lowest combustible ignition temperature. Imported room gas mixes instantly within each layer. Door states are fixed at load. Ceiling panels do not open the roof or alter ventilation. Legacy floorplan fires are ignored. Oxygen depletion, wind, window breakage and structural load paths are not solved. Room heat release is fuel-driven; do not use this model to infer ventilation-limited fire safety.

ignitions.time_s_reason: Ignition relative to fire clock. Delayed sources model a secondary ignition after entry.
ignitions.radius_m_reason: Radius of fuel initially involved, in metres. This changes the world fire size, never the robot response threshold.

wood.justification: Estimate of 8 kg/m2 accessible wood, not the full structure. 330 C is within the USDA 300 to 400 C piloted ignition range.

carpet.justification: Estimated textile and backing load of 2.5 kg/m2 and effective piloted ignition at 300 C; composition is unknown.

paper_finish.justification: Estimated wallpaper plus adhesive mass of 0.18 kg/m2 of wall, ignition at 300 C. No hidden timber studs are assumed.

wood_panels.justification: Estimated 6 kg/m2 accessible wall panelling; 330 C follows the wood ignition range.

paint_finish.justification: Estimated thin combustible paint film of 0.08 kg/m2 and effective ignition at 350 C; substrate stays inert.

inert.justification: Zero combustible fuel for stone, tile, plaster, concrete, steel and ceramics. 1100 C is a finite sentinel, not an ignition claim; zero fuel prevents ignition.

upholstery.justification: Estimated 22 kg/m2 of foam, fabric and frame in a sofa or mattress footprint; effective piloted ignition at 300 C. No product test exists.

furniture_wood.justification: Estimated 18 kg/m2 accessible wood in furniture; piloted ignition at 330 C. Does not include metal or glass mass.

textiles.justification: Estimated 9 kg/m2 of clothing or rug, effective ignition at 300 C; fibre types are unknown.

books.justification: Estimated 35 kg/m2 books and wooden shelving in a narrow footprint; effective paper ignition at 300 C.

appliance_contents.justification: Estimated 1 kg/m2 of plastic, wiring or residual contents in otherwise metal appliances; effective ignition at 350 C. No gas supply or explosion is modelled.

water.latent_heat_kj_l_reason: Rounded 2257 kJ/kg latent heat at 100 C, taking 1 litre as 1 kg. Grimwood, Fire-fighting Flow-rate, January 2005, p.24, example 2. https://highrisefire.co.uk/docs/FLOW-RATE%20202004.pdf
water.sensible_heat_kj_l_reason: Rounded 4.183 kJ/kg/K times 80 K from 20 C to 100 C, with 1 litre approximated as 1 kg. Same source, p.24; its worked example starts at 18 C. Combined budget is 2590 kJ/litre.
water.application_efficiency_reason: Selected 50 percent effective hose-stream cooling, following Grimwood 2005, pp.26 to 28, especially example 6 for a jet nozzle. This is an estimate for this nozzle, not a measurement. https://highrisefire.co.uk/docs/FLOW-RATE%20202004.pdf
water.wet_seconds_per_litre_reason: Scenario estimate of 30 seconds of ignition inhibition per litre delivered to a cell, additive after the last application. NISTIR 6191 motivates fuel cooling and surface contact, but does not measure this dry-out coefficient. https://www.nist.gov/publications/fire-fighting-properties-nistir-6191
water._reason: Flow is shared equally across visible cone cell centres, including cold fuel. Tick-interval overlap conserves litres for non-grid times. Exact room boundaries block water except within current door widths; no furniture occlusion. Flame heat is absorbed first; surplus cools toward ambient using gas.effective_heat_capacity_kj_m2_k times cell area, the existing effective heated-lining capacity. There is no separate solid-cell capacity in this model. Smoke and room gas use the remaining heat release. Wetting is a dry-out timer, not moisture transport or a validated suppression model. Sources accessed 2026-10-21.

collapse.note: Estimate for local ceiling-panel fall after sustained hot-gas exposure. Concrete ceiling excluded. Continuous exposure resets below the threshold. Protect full 0.9 m approach strips inside rooms on both sides of every door, including closed doors; this is not a proof of a navigable path after physical debris.

sources.justification: 0.25 m grid and 0.1 s step are numerical choices. One sofa ignition at (3,1.25) m at 0 s with radius 0.3 m is an estimated scenario choice. Furniture footprints are estimates, clipped to their room. Surface names and landmark kinds come from floorplan.json and props.json. All room boundaries must align to the grid.

20 C ambient is a scenario choice. NIST describes flashover with fire gases over 600 C and about 20 kW/m2 floor heat flux. Use 600 C as a gas-temperature trigger. 650 to 1100 C flame temperature and 1100 C hard bound are selected plausible ranges, not material-specific measurements. Flashover timing depends on ventilation and contents; the requested 180 to 300 s is a calibration target, not a universal rule.

USDA Wood Handbook chapter 18 gives 300 to 400 C surface temperatures before piloted wood ignition. Wood values of 330 C use that range. Other ignition values and every fuel density are estimates, documented in each material. No source certifies these particular household objects.

CFAST motivates hot upper and cooler lower room layers; this code does not implement CFAST. Every coefficient is estimated. Effective heat capacity 6.5 kJ/m2/K includes entrained gas and heated linings. Loss 0.055 kW/m2/K is an effective room heat loss. Convective heat fraction 0.65, exchange 3.5 internal and 0.4 external m3/s per metre of opening, gas capacity 1.2 kJ/m3/K, entrainment 0.0012 m3/s/kW are coarse choices. Initial layer depth 0.05 m and minimum height 0.4 m avoid zero volume. Lower heat fraction 0.12 and lower smoke fraction 0.08 preserve stratification. Smoke production 0.012 density*m3 per full-intensity burning cell per second, reference volume 1 m3 and decay 0.002/s define a dimensionless visual density, not soot concentration or visibility. Door exchange is multiplied by the fraction of the opening below the lower of the two layer interfaces; no hot gas crosses above a door head. The 3.5 value corresponds to a few m/s in a 2.1 m high opening and is an estimate. Heat capacity and exchange were selected using standalone default-house timing diagnostics, not experiments.

NIST experiments establish that upholstery and construction details change growth; they do not supply these coefficients. All spread constants are estimates: neighbour exchange 0.028/s, cooling 0.012/s, effective upper-gas radiation coupling 0.05/s, post-flashover heating 18 C/s, burn flux 0.018 kg/m2/s, ramp 8 s, relaxation 4 s, fuel variation +/-8%, effective heat of combustion 18000 kJ/kg. Query heating takes the maximum contribution of nearby same-room flames, with inverse-square horizontal falloff clipped at 1.5 m and a vertical plume scale 1.5 m. Peak added heating 450 C is an estimate. A half door uses half its opening width; closed doors have no leakage or failure. Surface radiation uses upper-layer gas temperature even when the lower air stays cooler; 0.05/s is an estimated 20 s thermal response for exposed finishes and furnishings.

650 C for 45 continuous seconds, six events total and at least 8 s between events are unvalidated ceiling-panel scenario rules, not a structural failure correlation. The 0.9 m protected width follows the floorplan clear-path rule. Only plaster ceilings may shed panels; collapse does not consume fuel or remove walls.

ignitions_reason: World-only ignition geometry and timing for a repeatable trigger experiment. Fuel, heat transfer, water physics and robot thresholds are unchanged. Radius sets the initially involved fuel area; later intensity follows the original fuel model.
